name: Falling Star
description: Summon a volatile Falling Star with a natural 3d10 Power roll and a modified 1d20 Accuracy roll.

lines: You summon a Falling Star. A tiny speck of light appears overhead, completely misses your foe, and disappears into the distance. Nobody says anything.
A very small star descends from above and misses spectacularly. Somehow, the lack of damage feels secondary to the embarrassment.
A respectable Falling Star streaks through the sea with impressive confidence and terrible aim. It explodes harmlessly nearby, as if hoping nobody noticed.
You summon a perfectly decent star and send it sailing past your foe. The star did its part. Your aim has declined to comment.
A colossal star tears through the Astral Sea with terrifying force... several feet to your foe's left. The resulting explosion is incredible. Your aim was not.
The sea erupts as an enormous star crashes down with enough power to annihilate almost anything. Unfortunately, your foe wasn't standing over there.
You summon what may genuinely be the most terrifying star you've ever created. It misses. You would prefer if nobody discussed this.
A tiny star wobbles toward your foe and barely clips them on the way past. Technically, that counts.
A suspiciously unimpressive star grazes your foe before drifting away. You briefly consider pretending that was intentional.
A decently powerful star descends at a deeply mediocre angle, clipping your foe before crashing nearby. It worked, which feels generous.
Your Falling Star carries respectable force and only a passing interest in Accuracy. It grazes your foe, then exits dramatically.
An enormous star screams toward your foe with terrifying force... and clips them on the edge before exploding somewhere behind them. Close enough?
A devastating star tears through the battlefield and barely grazes your foe. Somewhere, astronomy itself seems disappointed.
A tiny star descends directly onto your foe's head with impeccable accuracy. It wasn't very powerful, but the aim was honestly incredible.
You summon an absolutely pathetic little star and land it perfectly. You're not sure whether to be proud.
A solid Falling Star drops cleanly onto your foe and bursts in a bright flash. That worked. No cosmic embarrassment required.
Your star arrives with respectable power, respectable aim, and absolutely no complications. A suspiciously competent performance.
A massive star crashes directly into your foe and erupts in a violent burst of Astral light. No tricks. No complications. You simply hit them with a star.
A huge Falling Star descends exactly where intended and detonates with frightening force. Operating heavy Astral objects appears to be going alarmingly well.
You perfectly aimed... a really crappy star.
Your aim was flawless. Your star was not. Somehow, this still counts as a critical.
A tiny star strikes the exact perfect spot with incredible precision. If only you had remembered to summon a better star.
Your Falling Star strikes with perfect precision, bursting against your foe in a brilliant explosion of Astral light. Okay. That one was actually pretty good.
The star crashes directly into its target and erupts in a shower of brilliant light. For once, everything went according to plan.

The Astral Sea erupts with light as a colossal star tears through the water and crashes directly into your foe. The explosion sends starlight across the battlefield. You briefly wonder if that was excessive. It was.
An enormous star appears overhead. Your foe looks at the star. Then at you. Then back at the star. There is just enough time for regret.
You summon an absolutely enormous Falling Star and, against all reasonable expectations, aim it perfectly. The resulting explosion suggests you should probably not be trusted with astronomy.

naturalTwentyFlavor: The star lands with impossible precision. Somewhere in the Astral Sea, a Jellyfish gives you an approving wobble.
For once, the universe, the star, and your aim are all cooperating. This feels suspicious.
highPowerNaturalOneFlavor: You rolled enough Power to ruin someone's entire afternoon. Unfortunately, it was not your foe's afternoon.
